raw_response:
My first option to try would be **Vivaldi for Android**, using its ordinary Google Play release. It is the strongest documented match for the particular problem you described: Vivaldi's Android interface help explicitly places a Reload control in the address bar and explains how to keep the browser controls visible while scrolling. That is more useful here than a general claim that a browser has a pleasant interface. [Interface documentation](https://help.vivaldi.com/android/android-appearance/android-vivaldi-mobile-interface/)

I would configure it with the **address bar at the top** and enable **Settings → Appearance & Theme → Show Toolbars While Scrolling**. The same documentation notes that moving the bars to the bottom can put some controls in the menu because of limited space, so the top-bar configuration is the clearest documented starting point for keeping reload easy to reach. Whether that arrangement feels comfortable on your phone is still a personal usability check; I have not run the app on your device. [Interface and visibility settings](https://help.vivaldi.com/android/android-appearance/android-vivaldi-mobile-interface/)

Vivaldi also has documented built-in tracker and ad blocking, with controls for individual sites. Choose an enabled blocking level during setup; stronger levels can affect site behavior, so the existence of more aggressive blocking should not be mistaken for a guarantee that every site remains convenient to use. Its official installation guide describes installing directly from Google Play and currently lists Android 10 as the minimum supported version. No source build or alpha channel is needed for that route. [Privacy controls](https://help.vivaldi.com/android/android-privacy/android-tracker-and-ad-blocker/) · [Installation](https://help.vivaldi.com/android/android-install/android-install-and-update-vivaldi-mobile/)

My ranked shortlist is:

1. **Vivaldi — the best documented fit for the reload issue.** It has affirmative documentation for privacy controls, normal Play installation, and a visible reload control in the proposed configuration. The unresolved part is whether you find its interface usable. I would try this one first, while treating that preference as unverified rather than promising you will like it.

2. **Brave — a plausible alternative if its interface suits you.** Its normal Play listing documents tracking protection and other privacy controls, and it is a ready-made app rather than a build project. Brave also documents Android menu and toolbar customization. However, the primary material I could actually inspect did not establish the present location and accessibility of Reload. I would therefore keep Brave on the shortlist with that check still open, rather than assert that it solves your exact complaint. [Google Play](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.brave.browser&hl=en_US) · [Android interface changes](https://brave.com/whats-new/android/)

3. **DuckDuckGo Browser — another privacy-oriented Play-store option to consider.** Its official Android help documents Google Play installation, tracker blocking, and increased encryption. That is enough to establish a relevant alternative, but not enough to verify the reload workflow. An attempted inspection of the public Android code was blocked; search snippets were not sufficient to confirm what the current installed release shows. Its interface and accessible reload control remain checks before adopting it. [Official Android browser help](https://duckduckgo.com/duckduckgo-help-pages/mobile/android)

For Vivaldi, the decisive remaining check is whether the documented top-bar layout with persistent controls is usable for you. For Brave and DuckDuckGo, also confirm that the normal Play build gives you a reload action you can easily reach from a scrolled page. An acceptable interface and accessible reload would strengthen their fit; an interface that does not meet your requirement would rule out that particular configuration. Missing evidence alone does not establish that a browser lacks the feature.

This is a documentation-based shortlist, not a hands-on usability comparison. I have not added requirements for extensions, desktop synchronization, a particular rendering engine, or a particular business model because your summary did not specify them. There is also a timing limit: the question is dated October 21, 2026, while the inspected Brave Play listing was updated November 19, 2026. The other principal help pages are live and undated. They support the documented options now, but do not establish an exact historical snapshot of every interface on the question date.
